title: Fraction charts of finite coproducts of twists over a graded ring
statement: Let A be any commutative ring with an N-grading 𝒜, r a natural number, and a:Fin r→Z. Let F be the finite coproduct of Proj.twist 𝒜 (a i) [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. Over every homogeneous basic open D₊(f) of positive degree, there is an additive injection α from F sections into Away f (Fin r→A). Its range is degreeZeroFractions [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions] for the shifted grading: a vector y has degree n when yᵢ lies in 𝒜_(aᵢ+n) if aᵢ+n≥0 and is zero otherwise. The maps α intertwine awayToSection scalars with the canonical homogeneous-localization algebra map. For a canonical restriction with g^e=h*f, e>0 and h homogeneous, a section represented by y/f^m maps to (h^m•y)/g^(e*m). This includes r=0, arbitrary integer shifts, and nilpotent f.

proof.text: By Definition 01MN (1) and Lemma 01M7 (2), sections of twist 𝒜 (a i) on D₊(f) identify additively and scalar-linearly with the equal-degree fractions of the shift A(a i). Equivalently a numerator of degree a i + m*b is paired with denominator f^m. If that integer degree is negative, its component is zero. All these identifications are compatible with restrictions by 01M7 (3).

Finite coproducts of sheaves of modules are also their finite products, and products are computed sectionwise. Localization commutes with the finite product of the underlying modules: send a fraction vector to its coordinate fractions; to invert this map, express each coordinate with a power f^(mᵢ), choose m=max mᵢ and multiply its numerator by f^(m-mᵢ). Equality of fractions is preserved; finitely many witnesses for localization equality can likewise be multiplied to obtain one common witness. Consequently the inverse induces an additive injection α of the coproduct sections into Away f (Fin r→A).

Multiplying the i-th numerator by f^(m-mᵢ) makes its degree a i+m*b, so each image lies in the prescribed shifted degree-zero fractions. Conversely any homogeneous numerator vector over a homogeneous power of f yields, coordinatewise, a section of each twist, proving range equality. The zero polynomial, zero numerator and empty family are included: for r=0 take numerator zero and denominator 1.

The scalar formula follows from coordinatewise multiplication in the localization and the S_(f)-linearity of the individual chart maps. For g^e=h*f, (g^e)^m=h^m*f^m, so each coordinate yᵢ/f^m maps to h^m*yᵢ/g^(e*m). Lemma 01M7 (3) identifies this with the sheaf restriction; equality of all coordinates gives the displayed vector formula.

theorem finite_twist_coproduct_fractions
    {A σ : Type v} [CommRing A] [SetLike σ A] [AddSubgroupClass σ A]
    (𝒜 : ℕ → σ) [GradedRing 𝒜] (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → ℤ) :
  ∃ alpha : ∀ (f : A) (b : ℕ),
    0 < b → f ∈ 𝒜 b →
    (∐ (fun i : Fin r ↦ twist 𝒜 (a i))).val.obj (op (basicOpen 𝒜 f))
      →+ LocalizedModule.Away f (Fin r → A),
  (∀ (f : A) (b : ℕ) (hb : 0 < b)
    (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 b),
    Function.Injective (alpha f b hb hf) ∧
    Set.range (alpha f b hb hf) = degreeZeroFractions
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝒜 n : Set _))
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ {y : Fin r → A | ∀ i,
        if 0 ≤ a i + n then
          y i ∈ 𝒜 (a i + n).toNat
        else y i = 0}) (Submonoid.powers f)) ∧
  (∀ (f : A) (b : ℕ) (hb : 0 < b)
    (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 b)
    (q : HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 f)
    (s : (∐ (fun i : Fin r ↦ twist 𝒜 (a i))).val.obj (op (basicOpen 𝒜 f))),
    alpha f b hb hf (awayToSection 𝒜 f q
      • s) = algebraMap
        (HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 f)
        (Localization.Away f) q • alpha f b hb hf s) ∧
  (∀ (f g : A) (b c : ℕ) (hb : 0 < b) (hc : 0 < c)
    (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 b)
    (hg : g ∈ 𝒜 c)
    (inc : basicOpen 𝒜 g ≤
      basicOpen 𝒜 f)
    (e t : ℕ) (h : A),
    0 < e → h ∈ 𝒜 t → g ^ e = h * f →
    ∀ (m : ℕ) (y : Fin r → A)
      (s : (∐ (fun i : Fin r ↦ twist 𝒜 (a i))).val.obj
          (op (basicOpen 𝒜 f))),
      alpha f b hb hf s = mk y (⟨f ^ m, ⟨m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers f) →
      alpha g c hc hg ((∐ (fun i : Fin r ↦
        twist 𝒜 (a i))).val.map
          (homOfLE inc).op s) =
        mk (h ^ m • y) (⟨g ^ (e * m), ⟨e * m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers g))
